entry.title: Treat a card suspended while studying as marked
entry.content:
Treat a card suspended while studying as marked

A card that does not work gets flagged and suspended. report only looked for flags, and
resolve only cleared them, so a fixed card lost its flag and stayed suspended: out of study
for good, and invisible to every later report. Four agentic-ai cards resolved on Sep 12
were still sitting there.

report now lists suspended cards as `suspended`, and resolve unsuspends what it clears
(--all includes them). Both leave `orphaned` cards alone - that suspension is the sync's,
so resolving an old id after moving its card to a new one keeps the old note out of study.

entry.title: Purge everything that is not authoring or reviewing
entry.content:
Purge everything that is not authoring or reviewing

One goal: write cards, sync them, fix what studying flags. Anything not in furtherance is
gone.

Removed: the limits and warnings system entirely - length is a judgement and a character
count was a bad proxy for it, so the author skill makes that call from the deck's
AUTHORING.md and the validator only reports whether a card is valid. The raw-HTML template
override, replaced by a single css: key, because restyling is all a deck ever needed. The
style: alias, now that all 573 cards say type:. The example deck, the design doc, and a
reference documenting an acquirer deleted two rounds ago.

Kept, because not all cards are equal: card_types with their own fields, which is how a
card carries audio, an image or a phonetic transcription; code and reverse; and the whole
ingestion path.

deck.yaml renames styles: to types:, which is breaking - a deck must be edited in step.

Acceptance test holds: both decks sync add 0, update 0, orphan 0.

entry.title: Make card types and their fields deck-defined
entry.content:
Make card types and their fields deck-defined

A card type is now a contract - requires, optional, cloze, fields - and the deck declares
its types. That replaces the hardcoded cloze-versus-front/back branch: which keys a card
must carry, may carry, and may not all come from the type it names.

The tool ships basic and cloze as an always-available floor; a deck's styles: and
card_types: extend it. A bare name gets the basic contract UNLESS it matches a shipped
name, which keeps that type. That exception is load-bearing rather than tidy: without it a
deck listing cloze bare routes its cloze cards onto the basic note type, which Anki cannot
do in place - 102 re-adds and 102 lost review histories on the agentic deck alone.

style: is a silent alias for type:, so not one of the existing cards was rewritten.

Field removal refuses. Anki's modelFieldRemove destroys that field's content on every note
with no undo, so when a deck stops declaring a field, sync reports what Anki still has and
names the two ways out - declare a new type, or remove it by hand. It never removes.

Note lookup now queries every model in note_types:, not the two shipped ones. This was the
most dangerous spot in the change: a model missing from that query makes its notes
invisible, so each is re-added as a duplicate and orphan detection silently stops seeing
them. It has a test.

Deck fields nest under fields: on a card, so Card keeps extra=forbid and a misspelled key
stays an error. They land before Feedback so the field you type into stays last. Per-field
limits nest under limits.fields: for the same reason - flat, a misspelled back_char would
become a limit on a field nobody has.

Acceptance test: agentic-ai and quebec-french both sync add 0, update 0, orphan 0.

entry.title: Record the design for deck-defined card types
entry.content:
Record the design for deck-defined card types

Seven rounds of grilling turned the brief into decisions. The shape: card types are
contracts (requires/optional/cloze/fields), the tool ships basic and cloze as an
always-available floor, a deck's list extends it, and a bare name matching a shipped type
resolves to that type rather than to basic.

That last rule is the one that matters. Without it a deck listing cloze bare would route its
cloze cards onto the basic note type, which Anki cannot do in place - 102 re-adds and 102
lost review histories on the agentic deck alone.

Not built yet. Rollout, acceptance test and the two answers the PR note has to carry - field
removal refuses, and note lookup queries every declared model - are all written down.

entry.title: Add release.py
entry.content:
Add release.py

The version lives in two manifests and an install is cached by version, so a push without
a bump reaches nobody - which is how three feature releases shipped to no one. This owns
both files and refuses a dirty tree, a non-increasing version, or manifests that already
disagree. It writes by targeted replacement rather than re-serialising, so formatting and
comments survive.

No version bump: a maintainer script changes nothing for an installed copy.

entry.title: Let a deck ship its own card templates (0.3.0)
entry.content:
Let a deck ship its own card templates (0.3.0)

The templates: key documented itself as overriding Anki templates and CSS, and only ever
read cards.css - the HTML was hardcoded and unreachable. It now reads six optional files,
any subset, falling back to the shipped template for whatever a deck leaves out.

An empty override file is an error rather than a blank card side, because Anki would
accept it and render nothing on every card of that note type.

This is safe only because note types are already named per deck: updateModelTemplates
rewrites the type on every sync, so an override that leaked across decks would rewrite
someone else's cards.

entry.title: Move deck guidance into three layers
entry.content:
Move deck guidance into three layers

A deck was carrying an AUTHORING.md whose content was mostly not deck-specific: of 126
lines in the agentic one, 7 were about that deck. The rest was universal card craft,
personal house style, schema documentation duplicating the README, and examples
duplicating the deck's own cards.

So deck.yaml gains audience, scope and avoid - three optional lines that are the only
prose most decks need. Universal craft lives in the author skill; house style goes in a
root ancci.yaml inherited by every deck in a repository. A deck that genuinely needs more
keeps an AUTHORING.md, which overrides the rest.

The example deck now has no AUTHORING.md at all, which is the shape a new deck should
copy.

entry.title: Work from the root of a repository of decks
entry.content:
Work from the root of a repository of decks

A session usually sits at the root and moves between decks, so --deck now takes a deck
name as well as a path, and decks.py lists what is there with card counts. Standing at a
root with no deck still refuses to guess, and names the decks it found.

All five skills now pick the deck first and pass it explicitly, because syncing or
authoring into the wrong deck is worse than asking.

entry.title: Drop the repository acquirer, and fix what the smoke tests found
entry.content:
Drop the repository acquirer, and fix what the smoke tests found

Cloning a repo and reading it is something an agent already does well, so the fetcher
and its guesses about where docs live are gone; references/repo.md says to clone and
read instead. A github.com URL is now simply a page, which renders the README anyway.
RepoSource stays: citing a repo at a commit is still a real citation.

Running the remaining acquirers against real inputs for the first time found two
defects, neither of which unit tests would have caught:

- An EPUB cover is a base64 data URI, and converting it put the whole encoded file in
  the note. Images are now replaced by their alt text or dropped.
- PDFs that position characters instead of writing spaces came out with 24% of tokens
  fused together - whole sentences as one word. An explicit, size-relative word gap
  takes that to zero.

Video needed no changes: timestamped windows, chapters and auto-caption detection all
worked against a real video.

entry.title: Add source ingestion
entry.content:
Add source ingestion

One entrypoint takes a URL, a YouTube link, a repository, a PDF, an EPUB or a text
file and works out the kind from the shape of what it is given. Extracted text is cached
under .ancci/ and never committed; distilling it into a research note is a reading job,
so the script stops at the raw text and the skill does the rest.

Acquirers are lazily imported, so reading a local file loads neither a video extractor
nor an HTTP client.

Two things measured rather than assumed, both of which contradicted what I first believed:

- The converter reads a code block's language only off language-/lang- on <pre> or <code>,
  never from an ancestor. A pre-pass copies it down where a site names it - but MkDocs
  Material as deployed on docs.astral.sh names it nowhere, so fences there arrive bare.
  Documented rather than papered over.
- MkDocs line-number anchors leak an empty link onto every line of every code block: 136
  in one page. An earlier synthetic test used an anchor with no href, which the converter
  drops by itself, so it passed while the real markup was mangled. The regression test now
  uses the markup that actually ships.

entry.title: Package ancci as a Claude Code plugin
entry.content:
Package ancci as a Claude Code plugin

The package becomes standalone scripts over a shared _lib, each declaring its own
dependencies inline so uv builds the environment on first run and nobody installs
anything. validate.py needs only pydantic and pyyaml; the review commands need no
Markdown renderer, which is why fetch_notes moved out of sync and the exception types
moved into a module that imports nothing.

Four skills: new-deck and author run only when asked for by name, review and sync can
also be triggered in plain English. add-source waits for the ingestion work rather than
shipping a skill that calls scripts that do not exist yet.

Adds the plugin manifest, a marketplace entry so it installs from GitHub, MIT licence,
and a coffee-brewing example deck that overrides the default styles - the tool shipping
proof that it is not only for software.

entry.content:
Move the deck out to its own repo

The deck now lives in a separate decks repository with its authoring history intact; this
repo keeps only the tooling. Nothing about one subject is left in it.

The deck's own history stays here too - these paths were removed, not rewritten - so
git log still answers questions about how a card got the way it is.
